title: Two dreams, two endings, told with care.
subtitle: Yusuf delivers good news and hard news gently

row.title: one of you
sub: softened for the one who grieves

then: Yusuf told them: one of you will pour wine for his master, the other will be crucified. Ibn Kathir notes he {idea}did not address either man directly{/idea}, so the second would grieve less. When they claimed they had seen nothing, he said {trap}the matter is decided.{/trap}
now: The doctor who has to give bad news in the corridor. The manager telling a team about layoffs. You have to tell a friend something they will not want to hear. {idea}Truth does not have to be delivered like a blow.{/idea}
old: Honesty means saying it straight, however it lands.
new: I can tell the whole truth and still choose words that spare the heart.
try: Before you share difficult news with someone today, take one breath and soften the first sentence.

title: Mention me to your master, he asked, but he forgot.
subtitle: A small request, forgotten for years
then: Yusuf knew which man would go free and asked him: {idea}mention me to your king.{/idea} But the man {trap}forgot, a plot of Shaytan{/trap}, and Yusuf stayed in prison for several more years. Mujahid and Qatadah said the word used means between three and nine years.
now: You sent the CV and the contact promised to pass it on. You asked a cousin to put in a word. Months pass. Nothing. {idea}People forget. Allah does not.{/idea} Your name is still on His list.
old: If the person I counted on forgets me, I am stuck.
new: People forget, but the delay can be leading to a better door.
try: Think of a favor someone promised and forgot. Forgive it quietly and make dua for the outcome.

title: The king dreamed, and his whole court was lost.
subtitle: Seven fat cows, seven lean ones
then: The king of Egypt saw a dream that left him {trap}astonished and afraid{/trap}. He gathered priests, chiefs and princes and asked them to explain it. Ibn Kathir says Allah made this dream {idea}the reason for Yusuf's release{/idea}, with his honor preserved.
now: A problem lands on the desk of the most powerful person in the building, and nobody can solve it. You, in the back office, might have the answer. {idea}Allah can turn someone else's worry into your opening.{/idea}
old: The powerful people have nothing to do with my little situation.
new: Allah can move a king's sleep to open a prisoner's door.
try: Write down one closed door in your life and leave it with Allah in dua tonight.

title: Mixed-up dreams, the experts said, and we do not know.
subtitle: The court brushes off what it cannot explain
then: The king's advisers had no answer. Ibn Kathir says that {trap}as an excuse{/trap}, they called it a jumble of false dreams. They added that they were not skilled in interpreting dreams. {idea}Their failure set the stage{/idea} for the man who knew Yusuf to remember.
now: In the meeting, someone asks a question no one can answer, so the room decides it was a silly question. You do it too, with a hard question from your child. {idea}I do not know is a better answer than it does not matter.{/idea}
old: If I cannot explain it, it probably means nothing.
new: Not knowing is honest, dismissing the question to hide it is not.
try: The next time you do not know an answer today, simply say I do not know.

title: After years, the forgetful man finally remembered.
subtitle: The right memory at the right moment

row.title: the freed man
sub: I can tell you, send me

row.title: too late
sub: he should have spoken years ago

then: The man who had left prison {trap}forgot Yusuf for years{/trap}. Now, hearing the court fail, he remembered. Ibn Kathir says he told the king and his circle: {idea}I will tell you its meaning, so send me{/idea} to Yusuf, the man of truth.
now: You applied years ago and heard nothing. Then one day the call comes, exactly when the company is desperate. {reward}The memory came back when it would count most.{/reward} {idea}Delays are not always denials.{/idea}
old: If it did not happen when I wanted, it was never going to.
new: Allah brings the forgotten thing back to mind at the moment it matters most.
try: Message one person you forgot to follow up with. Today might be their right moment.

title: He called him the man of truth.
subtitle: Yusuf's reputation survived the prison walls
then: The freed man went to the prison and greeted Yusuf as {reward}the man of truth{/reward}. He repeated the king's dream word for word so he could {idea}return to the people and they might know.{/idea} The man who had forgotten Yusuf still remembered his character.
now: Years after you left a job, a former colleague still says: ask them, they are honest. {reward}That is the reputation that outlives the CV.{/reward} The title people give you when you are not in the room.
old: Being stuck somewhere low erases who I am.
new: A truthful character keeps its name, even inside a prison.
try: Keep one small promise today exactly as you said it, even if no one checks.

title: Sow for seven years, store it, and eat a little.
subtitle: Yusuf turns a dream into a plan
then: Yusuf explained the dream {idea}without blaming the man for forgetting him{/idea} and without asking for release first. Ibn Kathir says the cows were years. He advised them to {reward}store the harvest in its ears{/reward} to keep it healthy, eat only what they needed, and avoid extravagance.
now: Payday. The bonus. The good month at the shop. {trap}It is tempting to spend it all because times are good.{/trap} {idea}Yusuf's advice: enjoy a little, save the rest in a way that lasts.{/idea}
old: When things are good, I can relax and spend.
new: The good years are the time to prepare for the hard ones.
try: Put aside one small amount today, money, food, or time, for a harder day.

title: Then seven hard years will eat what you saved.
subtitle: The lean cows explained

row.title: the store saved them
sub: that is what it was for

then: Yusuf told them {trap}seven years of drought{/trap} would follow, the lean cows eating the fat ones. Ibn Kathir says nothing planted then would grow. They would live on {reward}what they had stored{/reward}, except a little they kept back.
now: The emergency fund that goes in one month when the car breaks and the boiler fails. It feels like it vanished. {reward}It did exactly its job.{/reward} {idea}Saving is not lost when a hard season uses it up.{/idea}
old: If my savings get used up, it was all for nothing.
new: What I stored in good times is what carries me through hard ones.
try: Thank Allah for one past hard season that something you prepared got you through.

title: After the drought, a year of rain and pressing.
subtitle: Good news the dream did not even show
then: Yusuf added something the king had not asked about. Ibn Kathir says he gave them {reward}good news{/reward}: after the years of drought would come a year of {idea}abundant rain{/idea}, when the land would produce again and people would press oil and grapes as usual.
now: The year of chemo. The long unemployment. The season of grief. {trap}It feels like it will never lift.{/trap} {reward}Yusuf's answer ends with rain.{/reward} Hard years are counted, not endless.
old: This hard season is just how life is now.
new: Hardship has a number, and after it comes rain.
try: Tell someone going through a hard time one hopeful thing you truly believe.

title: Freedom was offered, and he said: first clear my name.
subtitle: Yusuf refuses to leave until the truth is known
then: The king wanted Yusuf brought to him. Ibn Kathir says Yusuf {idea}refused to leave until his innocence was declared{/idea}, so all would know the prison was an injustice. The Prophet ﷺ praised his patience, saying that if he had stayed in prison as long, {reward}he would have accepted the offer{/reward}.
now: You were let go after a false complaint. Now they want you back, quietly, no questions asked. {idea}Sometimes the right move is to ask for the record to be corrected first.{/idea} Your name matters, not just your exit.
old: When a door opens, grab it before it closes.
new: Leaving with my name cleared can be worth more than leaving early.
try: If there is a misunderstanding about you, ask calmly for it to be cleared, without anger.

title: Now the truth is out: it was I who tried.
subtitle: The confession, years later

row.title: the women
sub: we know no evil of him

then: The king gathered the women who cut their hands and asked what happened. They said: {idea}Allah forbid, we know no evil against him.{/idea} Then the 'Aziz's wife said: {reward}now the truth is plain.{/reward} It was I who sought to seduce him, and he is truthful.
now: Years after the falling out, the person who spread the story finally admits it was not true. Or you are the one who should admit it. {idea}The truth has a way of coming out, and saying it yourself is a mercy.{/idea}
old: Too much time has passed for the truth to matter now.
new: It is never too late for the truth to come out, even from my own mouth.
try: If you once told a story that hurt someone unfairly, correct it with one person this week.

title: Allah does not let the betrayers' plan succeed.
subtitle: The confession and why it was made
then: Ibn Kathir's stronger view is that the 'Aziz's wife continued: I admit this {idea}so my husband knows I did not betray him in his absence{/idea}, and nothing happened. Others said Yusuf said these words. Either way, the verse sets a rule: {trap}Allah does not guide the plot of the betrayers.{/trap}
now: The colleague who undermines you in emails you never see. The secret you are keeping from your spouse. {trap}Plots built on betrayal seem to work for a while.{/trap} {idea}They never get where they wanted to go.{/idea}
old: If no one finds out, it does not matter.
new: Betrayal behind someone's back has no path to real success.
try: Do one thing today you would be fine with the other person seeing.

title: I do not claim my self is innocent.
subtitle: The soul pulls toward wrong, unless Allah has mercy
then: In Ibn Kathir's stronger view, the 'Aziz's wife said: {idea}I do not free myself from blame.{/idea} The soul wishes and desires, and that is what drove her. She ended with hope: {reward}my Lord is Forgiving, Most Merciful.{/reward}
now: You snapped at your kids, then blamed the traffic. You scrolled what you should not, then blamed the algorithm. {idea}Owning it is the first step back.{/idea} And the One you return to is Forgiving.
old: I only did it because of the situation I was in.
new: My own self pulls me toward wrong, and only Allah's mercy keeps me.
try: Tonight, name one mistake from today without an excuse, and ask Allah to forgive it.
